title: Bay services.yml
description: Schema for the Bay framework services.yml configuration file.

services.description: Service definitions — containers with Traefik routing and SSL.

propertyNames.description: A service name becomes a container name, a Traefik router name, a default database name and a shell word in rebuild.sh. Constrain it once, here.
An accessory name reaches `docker exec` in the generated backup script. Same constraint as a service name.

jobs.description: Scheduled one-shot jobs, compiled from bay.toml [[jobs]]. Keyed by the job container name. The deploy renders a script and a systemd timer per job on the box that runs `of`.

of.description: The container whose image, env file, network and mounts the job uses.

schedule.description: The five-field cron line from bay.toml, UTC.

on_calendar.description: The same schedule as a systemd OnCalendar expression, UTC.

volume_backups.description: Volume mounts with backup true, compiled from bay.toml mounts. Keyed by the volume name. The backup role adds a restic file backup <stack_name>_<volume> on the box that runs `container`.

container.description: The container that mounts the volume. The backup reads the volume through it.

path.description: Where the volume is mounted in the container.

schedule.description: Daily, at the [backup] hour, UTC. Absent: backup_schedule.

retain.description: Days to keep, from [backup] keep. Absent: backup_retain.

tailnet_proxies.description: Tailnet routes, compiled from [tailnet.routes] in bay.fleet.toml. Read by the traefik, headscale and crowdsec templates on the ingress box.

^_.description: Reserved scratch keys (e.g. _anchors) for YAML anchor declarations. Ignored by the framework.

path.description: bay.toml path: route only this path prefix of `domains` (the main domains), on a / boundary. The router outranks the main container's router. The prefix is not stripped.

regions.description: Region restriction. Empty or absent means all regions.

depends_on.description: Service/accessory names this service depends on.

healthcheck_path.description: Path probed by `bay healthcheck`. Use a route that exercises the dynamic backend (e.g. `/healthcheck`) when nginx and the app share a container — probing `/` would return nginx's static response even if the app process is dead.

config_files.description: Config files to copy into the stack directory.

config_files_mode.description: Permissions for this definition's config_files. 'private' (default): files 0640, directories 0750, readable by the deploy user and the docker group only. 'public': files 0644, and config/ plus every directory on the way to them 0755, so a container that runs as a uid outside the docker group can read them. Only for files that hold no secret.

public_routes.description: Routes exempt from VPN restriction (for vpn-access services). Traefik matches a route inside a backquoted string, which has no escape sequence, so backtick / quote / dollar / semicolon / backslash / newline are rejected here. A bare "/" matches this pattern but is rejected by `bay validate` — it makes the whole vpn service public.

vpn_routes.description: Routes protected by VPN on an otherwise public service. Same charset as public_routes.

release.description: bay.toml release: a shell command run once in a one-shot container of the new image before the container is created or recreated. A failure stops that container's deploy and the old container stays.

zero_downtime.description: Enable canary zero-downtime deploy. Default false (opt-in).

memswap_limit.description: Container memory plus swap limit (e.g., '512m'). Set it equal to mem_limit to give the container no swap, so its pages never reach disk. Requires mem_limit and must not be smaller than it. '-1' means unlimited swap.

health_check_timeout.description: How long this service may take to become healthy after a restart, in seconds. Two consumers: (1) rebuild.sh's post-restart health poll, which decides when to roll back — must be >= healthcheck.start_period, and has no effect if no healthcheck block is configured; (2) the post-deploy `bay healthcheck` URL probe's readiness window, where it can only widen the 90s framework default (a smaller value is ignored so the probe never gets stricter than baseline). Overrides git_deploy_health_check_timeout for this service. Default: 90 (group_vars) or framework default.

port.description: Host port binding. Prefer declaring the IP via `expose:` (loopback | tailnet | host) so the bind IP lives alongside the accessory. When both are set, `expose:` wins and any IP prefix in `port:` is replaced.

expose.description: Which host interface the accessory's port binds to. `loopback` (default) = 127.0.0.1; `gateway` = the active access gateway's overlay IP (`gateway_bind_ip`; deploy fails if the backend provides none). `tailnet` is a permanently-supported synonym for `gateway`, kept so existing services.yml files never need editing; `host` = 0.0.0.0 (explicit external exposure — unusual, expect reviewer friction).

expose_host_ack.description: Required acknowledgement for `expose: host`. A host-published port is DNAT'd in PREROUTING and never reaches the nftables `input` chain, so it is never seen by the CrowdSec bouncer. `bay validate` fails on `expose: host` unless this flag is true. Setting it changes nothing about the rendered port binding — it records a reviewed acceptance of the bypass.

release.description: bay.toml release: a shell command run once in a one-shot container of the new image before the container is created or recreated. A failure stops that container's deploy and the old container stays.

config_files_mode.description: Permissions for this definition's config_files. 'private' (default): files 0640, directories 0750, readable by the deploy user and the docker group only. 'public': files 0644, and config/ plus every directory on the way to them 0755, so a container that runs as a uid outside the docker group can read them. Only for files that hold no secret.

memswap_limit.description: Container memory plus swap limit (e.g., '512m'). Set it equal to mem_limit to give the container no swap, so its pages never reach disk. Requires mem_limit and must not be smaller than it. '-1' means unlimited swap.

health_check_timeout.description: Rebuild.sh post-restart health poll timeout in seconds. Must be >= healthcheck.start_period. Has no effect if no healthcheck block is configured. Overrides git_deploy_health_check_timeout for this service. Default: 90 (group_vars) or framework default.

strategy.description: Build strategy: local (build on server), remote (build on build server, push to registry, server pulls), or registry (pull pre-built image from external CI). 'push' is a deprecated alias for 'remote'. Defaults to git_deploy_build_strategy.

dockerfile.description: Dockerfile path relative to repo root.

context.description: Build context path relative to repo root.

secrets.description: Build secrets — name to vault key mapping.

token.description: Vault key for git access token (private repos).

shared_from.description: The main container whose build this one shares (bay.toml: a service with neither image nor build). The main container builds; this one re-tags its image.

track.description: Written by bay compile from [deploy.<env>] track. Absent means branch: a push builds and deploys. pin: a push builds and tags the image by commit, and only bay up deploys.

frozen.description: Written by bay compile while bay rollback froze the environment: a push builds and tags, never deploys.

bay_toml_hash.description: Canonical hash of the pinned bay.toml (bay_reconcile.tomlhash). Only for a project whose bay.toml lives in the app repo. A push whose bay.toml hashes differently is held until bay up.

bay_build_hash.description: Canonical hash of what the image is built from in the pinned bay.toml: [build], image and their per-env and per-service overrides (python -m bay_reconcile.tomlhash --section build). Written next to bay_toml_hash. A push whose bay.toml has another build hash is never config only: it builds, and the hold guard holds it.

bay_toml_path.description: Where the bay.toml lives in the app repo, for the hold guard.

bay_toml_files.description: The files the bay.toml mounts (from = ..., not fleet:), relative to the app repo root. A push that changes only these and bay_toml_path is config only: rebuild.sh neither builds nor deploys it; bay up does.

exclude.description: Gitignore-style glob patterns. Skip rebuild if ALL changed files match.

include.description: Reserved for future use. Not yet supported.

expose.description: Which host interface the service's internal port binds to. Optional — by default Traefik-fronted services have no host binding (reachable only inside the docker network). `loopback` = 127.0.0.1; `gateway` = the active access gateway's overlay IP (`gateway_bind_ip`; deploy fails if the backend provides none). `tailnet` is a permanently-supported synonym for `gateway`, kept so existing services.yml files never need editing; `host` = 0.0.0.0 (explicit external exposure — bypasses Traefik, expect reviewer friction). Required when another service in another region declares `links:` to this service.

expose_host_ack.description: Required acknowledgement for `ports.expose: host`. A host-published port is DNAT'd in PREROUTING and never reaches the nftables `input` chain, so it is never seen by the CrowdSec bouncer. `bay validate` fails on `expose: host` unless this flag is true. Setting it changes nothing about the rendered port binding — it records a reviewed acceptance of the bypass.

clear.description: Plain-text environment variables. Keys are POSIX environment variable names.

secret.description: Secret environment variables — list of key names or key-to-vault mapping.

source_path.description: In-container path the `file` method backs up (docker cp source; also the restore target). Defaults to /data.

paths.description: Reserved for future use — not currently read by any backup method. The `file` method takes its in-container path from `source_path`, a separate key.

accessory.description: Name of the database accessory to bind to.

name.description: Database name (defaults to service name). PostgreSQL identifier charset: roles/deploy_stack/tasks/database_provision.yml interpolates it into SQL.

user.description: Database user (defaults to service name). PostgreSQL identifier charset — see database.name.

log_rotation.description: Per-container docker log retention. Either `false` (opt out, inherit daemon log-opts) or a partial override of log_rotation_defaults.

max_file.description: Number of rotated log files to retain.

log_retention.description: Opt-in host-side log archival with time-based retention. Archives land under /opt/<stack>/logs/services/<svc>/ and survive container recreation. Orthogonal to `log_rotation`; both can coexist on one container. Requires a compatible docker log driver (json-file or local).

days.description: Archive retention window in days. Daily rotation writes YYYY-MM-DD.log.gz; files older than this are alerted and pruned at 00:00 UTC.

max_total_size.description: Hard ceiling on the archive directory size (e.g. '500m', '2g'). Sum across host validated at deploy time against log_retention_budget_fraction * log_retention_disk_bytes.

mode.description: 'normal' (default): 0640, group-readable by the app-owner's log group. 'sensitive': 0600 root:root — the app-owner's log group cannot read. Use 'sensitive' for services that log detailed PII.
